summaryDeep: You think and talk in ways that keep catching on each other. Similar enough to engage constantly, different enough to misread. Slow down and check what they actually meant.
tension: The challenge is that repeated misunderstandings can slowly put both people on guard. Over time, you stop entering conversations with curiosity and start entering them with expectation. A normal question can sound like doubt. A pause can feel like judgment. A simple clarification can land as rejection. Before long, the conversation is carrying the weight of every previous misunderstanding before it has even had a chance to unfold.
advice: This is where the real work begins. When communication breaks down, the temptation is to turn one difficult moment into a larger conclusion about the relationship. Resist that impulse. Slow the conversation down. Get curious before you get certain. Ask what they meant. Share what you heard. Check the story you are telling against what is actually happening. The goal is not perfect communication. The goal is to keep returning to clarity instead of punishing each other for the places where the message got distorted.
summaryShort: You think and talk in ways that keep catching on each other.
